log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Mega: Gengar. Gengar-Mega walls Sneasler (Fake Out/Close Combat immune, Dire Claw 0.25x) and Kleavor (Bug 0.25x, CC immune) — only Blastoise-Mega Dark Pulse threatens. Expecting opponent to adjust with Kleavor+Clefable per G1 notes. Lead Gengar+Klefki: Gengar Protects T1 to safely Mega Evolve (immune to Fake Out regardless), Klefki sets Reflect via Prankster for physical mitigation. Shadow Tag then traps opponents — Kleavor/Sneasler cannot switch and cannot damage Gengar. Back Serperior+Gyarados
decisions.notebook: G2 plan: Gengar-Mega lead if no Blastoise-Mega. KEY DISCOVERY: Gengar (Ghost/Poison) walls Sneasler (Fake Out immune, Close Combat immune, Dire Claw 0.25x) AND Kleavor (X-Scissor/U-turn 0.25x, Close Combat immune, only Stone Axe neutral 65 BP). Only Blastoise-Mega Dark Pulse (2x SE) threatens Gengar-Mega. Shadow Tag traps both — they cannot switch out. Klefki resists Kleavor (Bug 0.25x, Rock 0.5x) and provides Prankster screens/Thunder Wave. If opponent repeats Blastoise-Mega: pivot to Serperior (Leaf Storm possible OHKO on Blastoise-Mega 55-121%) and use Light Screen to potentially let Gengar survive Dark Pulse. Serperior Leaf Storm possible OHKO on Hippowdon (65-148%). Aegislash Sacred Sword is 0.5x NVE into Sneasler (Fighting vs Fighting/Poison) — do not rely on it for Sneasler. Gyarados takes 2x from Kleavor Stone Axe (not 4x — Rock vs Water/Flying = 1x*2x). For G3 if needed: Maushold (Follow Me+Helping Hand+Friend Guard) is alternative Gengar partner for pure offense; Aegislash King's Shield drops contact attackers' Attack but is slow and less synergistic.

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Blastoise-Mega. Lead Whimsicott and Sneasler to set Tailwind and threaten immediate pressure with Fake Out and Dire Claw/Close Combat. Blastoise-Mega and Hippowdon back provide Mega Launcher-boosted dark coverage and sand pressure to clean up the endgame.

Mega Evolve Gengar for Shadow Tag, trapping both foes. Sludge Bomb 4x SE guaranteed OHKOs Whimsicott (197-465%), removing Tailwind/Prankster support. Klefki Thunder Wave->Sneasler lands if Sneasler doesn't Fake Out (Prankster +1 beats Close Combat). If flinched, no loss—Gengar still KOs Whimsicott. Next turn Klefki TWaves Sneasler (priority), Gengar-Mega Psychics to break Focus Sash, then T3 Klefki Protects while Gengar KOs 1-HP Sneasler.
decisions.notebook: G2 T1 plan executing: Mega Gengar + Klefki lead. Sludge Bomb OHKOs Whimsicott (4x SE, 197-465%). Sneasler Close Combat does 39-84.8% to Klefki (survives one). Shadow Tag traps both. Turn 2: Klefki TWave Sneasler (Prankster priority beats CC), Gengar-Mega Psychic breaks Focus Sash+Unburden. Turn 3: Klefki Protect, Gengar-Mega KOs 1-HP Sneasler. Endgame: Gengar-Mega + Serperior/Gyarados vs opponent's 2 back Pokémon (Blastoise-Mega/Hippowdon/Kleavor/Clefable). If Blastoise-Mega appears, pivot Serperior for Leaf Storm. Gengar-Mega SpA 222, Spe ~200. Klefki Def 144 survives one Close Combat but not two without Reflect.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott uses Prankster Tailwind to guarantee outspeeding Mega Gengar next turn. Sneasler uses Fake Out on Klefki to disrupt potential Prankster screening or Thunder Wave, keeping Whimsicott and Sneasler safe and setting up optimal offensive pressure.

Whimsicott fainted, so we bring in Blastoise to threaten heavy damage with Mega-evolved dark/water moves while Tailwind is active. Sneasler stays active (passing slot 2) to maintain pressure and avoid bad matchups against Gengar's Psychic.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Mega Gengar (Timid, Gengarite, Sludge Bomb/Shadow Ball/Psychic/Protect), Klefki (Bold, Light Clay, Prankster, Reflect/Light Screen/Thunder Wave/Foul Play), Aegislash, and Gyarados. Sneasler's Unburden was triggered by Focus Sash consumption on turn 1. Blastoise-Mega leverages Mega Launcher-boosted dark/pulse attacks against Ghost/Steel threats.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler will likely Protect (avoids 4x SE Psychic + Prankster TWave). Blastoise Megas + Dark Pulse hits Gengar for 36-54% with Mega Launcher. Protect keeps Gengar at 100% preserving Shadow Tag. Klefki TWave Blastoise (Prankster +1 outspeeds) paralyzes it — effective speed drops to ~49-65 under Tailwind, far below Gengar's 200. Next turn Gengar outspeeds both foes and can Shadow Ball Blastoise (34-62%) or Psychic Sneasler. If Sneasler attacks instead, Klefki survives one Close Combat (93-65=28%
decisions.notebook: G2: Opponent leads Whimsicott+Sneasler w/ Tailwind+Fake Out. Sneasler: Focus Sash+Unburden, Jolly, raw Spe 154-189. Blastoise: Blastoisinite, Modest, raw Spe 98-130. Mega Launcher boosts Dark Pulse 1.5x (~36-54% on Gengar-Mega). Shadow Tag traps both non-Ghost foes. Plan: TWave Blastoise T2, then Gengar outspeeds paralyzed Blastoise to Shadow Ball (34-62%) or Psychic Sneasler (4x SE breaks Sash). Klefki survives one neutral Close Combat (46-65%). Endgame: Gengar-Mega+Serperior/Gyarados vs Hippowdon/Kleavor/Clefable. Serperior Leaf Storm for Blastoise-Mega if needed. Opponent uses Tailwind speed control; paralyzing key attackers under Tailwind is high-value.

decisions.rationale: Under Tailwind, Blastoise outspeeds Mega Gengar and hits it super-effectively with Mega Launcher-boosted Dark Pulse. Sneasler targets Klefki with Dire Claw or Close Combat to pressure the Prankster setter while avoiding Mega Gengar's Ghost/Poison immunities.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Gengar-Mega)
decisions.rationale: Dark Pulse + Mega Launcher can OHKO Gengar (tool omits abilities: 32-107% × 1.5 = ~48-160%). Light Screen (Prankster +1, before Blastoise) halves it to survivable ~24-80%. Shadow Ball chips Blastoise 23-70%. Klefki dies but provides guaranteed value. Keeping Gengar alive maintains Shadow Tag, trapping both foes. Next turn bring in Serperior/Gyarados and finish Blastoise or break Sneasler's Sash.
decisions.notebook: G2: Opponent leads Whimsicott+Sneasler w/ Tailwind+Fake Out. Sneasler: Focus Sash+Unburden, Jolly, raw Spe 154-189. Blastoise: Blastoisinite, Modest, raw Spe 98-130, Mega Launcher boosts Dark Pulse 1.5x (potential OHKO on Gengar-Mega without Light Screen). Shadow Tag traps both non-Ghost active foes — never switch Gengar out or opponent escapes. Klefki at 13% is expendable; best use is Prankster Light Screen or TWave. Plan: Light Screen T3 to protect Gengar, Shadow Ball Blastoise, then bring Serperior/Gyarados T4. Serperior Leaf Storm SE on Blastoise; Gyarados Intimidate lowers Sneasler Atk. Sneasler's attacks on Gengar are useless (CC immune, Dire Claw 0.25x) — Blastoise Dark Pulse is the real threat. Endgame: Gengar-Mega+Serperior/Gyarados vs Hippowdon/Kleavor/Clefable. Opponent uses Tailwind speed control; paralyzing key attackers under Tailwind is high-value.

decisions.rationale: Gengar-Mega used Protect last turn, so it can't protect reliably. Blastoise's Dark Pulse hits Gengar-Mega for super-effective damage (Mega Launcher boosted), and Sneasler protects to avoid any incoming Psychic or attack while Tailwind is active.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Mega Gengar (Timid, Gengarite, Sludge Bomb/Shadow Ball/Psychic/Protect) and Klefki (Bold, Light Clay, Prankster, Reflect/Light Screen/Thunder Wave/Foul Play).

decisions.rationale: Dark Pulse guaranteed KOs Gengar at 15% even through Light Screen, so Gengar must Protect. Switching Klefki(13%) to Gyarados brings Intimidate to neuter Sneasler's weak attacks. Tailwind expires next turn; Gengar(200) then outspeeds both foes and double-targets Blastoise with Gyarados for a guaranteed KO, leaving only Sash Sneasler whose attacks are useless vs this team.
decisions.notebook: G2: Blastoise-Mega Dark Pulse w/ Mega Launcher guaranteed KOs Gengar-Mega through Light Screen — Gengar must Protect when Blastoise is alive and could move. Shadow Ball on Blastoise w/ SpD-1 does ~45-96% (not guaranteed KO from 55%). After Tailwind expires, Gengar(200) outspeeds Sneasler(154-189) and Blastoise(49-65 par). Sneasler Dire Claw is 2x SE on Serperior — risky switch if Sneasler could outspeed(182-189). Gyarados Intimidate valuable for neutering Sneasler. Endgame plan: KO Blastoise first (double-target), then break Sneasler Sash + finish with second hit. Opponent trapped by Shadow Tag until Gengar faints.

decisions.rationale: Gengar is at 15% HP and Klefki is at 13%. Tailwind expires this turn. Sneasler is at -1 Def/-1 SpD and Gengar threatens 4x super-effective Psychic; switching Sneasler to Hippowdon brings in Sand Stream and a sturdy ground type safely, while Blastoise finishes Gengar with Dark Pulse.

Gengar at 15% and Klefki at 13% are both very low. Blastoise outspeeds Klefki and can KO with Dark Pulse (or Water Pulse), while Sneasler can finish Klefki with Close Combat or attack Gengar. Tailwind expires this turn, so we must secure the game immediately.

Double-target Blastoise: Gengar Shadow Ball (200 Spe, SpD-1 on foe ≈49-86%) + Gyarados Crunch (133 Spe, 18-33%) guarantees KO before paralyzed Blastoise (49-65) can Dark Pulse. Sneasler can't damage Gengar at all. If Blastoise Protects, Gengar still survives and we retry. Only real threat to Gengar eliminated this turn.
decisions.notebook: G2: Blastoise-Mega has SpD-1 from Sneasler's Close Combats — Shadow Ball damage ~1.5x higher than base estimate. Sneasler cannot damage Gengar-Mega at all (CC immune Ghost, Dire Claw 0.25x, Fake Out immune). Shadow Tag traps both foes — no switches possible while Gengar alive. Endgame: KO Blastoise this turn, then break Sneasler Sash + finish. Serperior and Klefki on bench for backup. Klefki at 13% — emergency switch only.

decisions.rationale: Gengar is at 15% HP and vulnerable to Dark Pulse, but used Protect last turn so it might protect again or switch. Sneasler is at -2 Def/-2 SpD and vulnerable to Gengar's Psychic (4x effective). Protecting Sneasler while Blastoise hits Gengar with Dark Pulse KOs or pressures Gengar, while avoiding a free KO on Sneasler.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Mega Gengar (Timid, Gengarite, Sludge Bomb/Shadow Ball/Psychic/Protect) and Klefki (Bold, Light Clay, Prankster, Reflect/Light Screen/Thunder Wave/Foul Play). Gyarados is Adamant with Life Orb. Light Screen is up on opponent side.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Both EQ and Rock Slide KO Gengar at 15%, so Protecting only delays while Sash stays intact. Psychic 4x SE (112-255%) breaks Sneasler's Sash guaranteed; Waterfall chunks Hippowdon 45-93%. Gengar dies but trade is overwhelming: Gyarados 76% + Serperior 100% vs 1-HP Sneasler + damaged Hippowdon. Even if Sneasler Protects (reduced rate), still winning 3v2.
decisions.notebook: G2 endgame plan: Gengar at 15% is dead to both Hippowdon EQ and Rock Slide — spending it to break Sneasler Sash via 4x Psychic is optimal. After Gengar falls, Gyarados Waterfall (2x SE on Hippowdon, 45-93%) + Serperior Leaf Storm (Contrary boosts SpA) clean up. Sneasler Focus Sash is the only obstacle; once broken at 1 HP it's trivial. Klefki at 13% is emergency-only. Opponent has no switches available (only 2 Pokemon left, both active).

decisions.rationale: Both fainted; must send Serperior and Klefki. Serperior outspeeds Hippowdon and Leaf Storm (2x SE + Expert Belt + Contrary SpA boost) cleans up 61% Hippowdon. Klefki at 13% is pure sack fodder—Thunder Wave is immune to Ground. Positioning is irrelevant since Hippowdon's only attacking moves are spread. Serperior slot 1, Klefki slot 2.
decisions.notebook: G2 endgame: Serperior (100%, Expert Belt, Contrary, Timid, 181 Spe) + Klefki (13%, Light Clay, Prankster, Bold, 95 Spe) vs Hippowdon (61%, Sitrus consumed, Sand Stream, Impish, 67-99 Spe). Serperior outspeeds and Leaf Storm 2x SE should KO. Klefki Thunder Wave useless vs Ground-type. Klefki is emergency sack only. If Hippowdon Protects, Serperior can Protect back or attack next turn—sand + Light Screen timer favors patience. Win condition: land Leaf Storm on Hippowdon. Opponent team: Sneasler (Sash/Unburden, fainted), Whimsicott (Prankster, fainted), Blastoise-Mega (par, fainted), Hippowdon (active), Kleavor (Scarf Sharpness, not brought), Clefable (Lefties Magic Guard, not brought). Opponent tends to Protect with Sneasler to stall and plays aggressively with Close Combat. G1 result: won. Series lead 1-0.

decisions.rationale: Gengar-Mega is at 15% and weak to Sandstorm, but has 4x super-effective Psychic against Sneasler and Protect. Rock Slide hits both foes and threatens Gyarados without hurting Sneasler (unlike Earthquake). Sneasler's Close Combat chunks Gyarados (resisted, but Sneasler has high base attack even at -1).
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Mega Gengar (Timid, Gengarite, Sludge Bomb/Shadow Ball/Psychic/Protect) and Klefki (Bold, Light Clay, Prankster, Reflect/Light Screen/Thunder Wave/Foul Play). Gyarados is Adamant with Life Orb.

decisions.rationale: Leaf Storm min roll 64.7% exceeds Hippowdon's 61% HP — guaranteed KO if it connects. Serperior outspeeds all non-priority moves. Only threat is Protect (priority +4), but even then I adapt next turn with 8 PP. Klefki Foul Play adds 8-18% chip as miss/Protect insurance. 90% accuracy is the only real risk; no safer line exists.
decisions.notebook: G2 endgame won if Leaf Storm lands on Hippowdon (guaranteed KO from 61%). Series lead 1-0. Opponent tends to Protect with low-health mons to stall. Kleavor (Scarf Sharpness) and Clefable (Lefties Magic Guard) were not brought G2 — may appear G3. Opponent plays aggressively with Close Combat and uses Protect to stall.

decisions.rationale: Hippowdon is alone against Serperior and Klefki. Rock Slide hits both foes and can chip down Klefki (at 13%) while dealing damage to Serperior. Earthquake hits Serperior for 0.5x and Klefki for 2x, but Rock Slide is safer for dual-target pressure.

Leaf Storm is a guaranteed KO from 48% (min 64.7%). 90% accuracy means likely instant win. Klefki's Prankster Thunder Wave lands first regardless of Klefki's 3% HP, giving paralysis insurance if Leaf Storm misses. Even on a miss, Serperior at 78% safely outspeeds and 2HKOs Hippowdon through any Slack Off healing. No reason to delay the KO shot.
decisions.notebook: G2: Hippowdon is last foe; Leaf Storm guaranteed KO from 48% with Serperior SpA 127 (min roll 64.7%). Series lead 1-0. Opponent tends to Protect with low-health mons. Kleavor (Scarf Sharpness) and Clefable (Lefties Magic Guard) not brought G2 — likely G3 options. Opponent plays aggressively with Close Combat, uses Protect to stall.

decisions.rationale: Hippowdon is at 49% HP and needs to heal with Slack Off against Serperior and Klefki (with Klefki at 3% and Serperior at 78%). Slack Off restores HP reliably while Sandstorm chips away at them.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Mega Gengar and Klefki with Prankster/Light Screen/Reflect/Thunder Wave/Foul Play. Serperior is Timid with ExpertBelt and Leaf Storm/Dragon Pulse/Protect/Taunt.

reflections.summary: Series closed 2-0. Gengar-Mega's Protect on turn 4 dodged Dark Pulse and let it KO Blastoise with Shadow Ball next turn, removing the opponent's Mega early. Gyarados softened Hippowdon with Waterfall before fainting, and Serperior cleaned up the weakened Hippowdon with Leaf Storm at +2 SpA. Opponent's Whimsicott lost Tailwind on turn 4, and Sneasler was chipped to its Focus Sash and finished by Psychic. The four brought and Gengar-Mega choice matched well: Shadow Ball hit Blastoise, Psychic hit
reflections.adjustment: Series is won 2-0; no next game. If continuing, avoid targeting Ground-types with Thunder Wave and preserve Klefki's HP better so it can set screens for more than one turn.
reflections.notebook: Series won 2-0. Opponent never brought Kleavor (Scarf Sharpness) or Clefable (Lefties Magic Guard) across both games — likely avoids them or saves for specific matchups. Opponent tends to Protect with low-health mons and plays aggressively with Close Combat. Opponent's Hippowdon is Ground-type (immune to Thunder Wave). Whimsicott Tailwind was lost to Shadow Tag on turn 4 — Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag disrupts Prankster Tailwind setup. Opponent's Blastoise-Mega is Modest with Water Pulse/Aura Sphere/Dark Pulse/Protect.

reflections.summary: Mega Blastoise and Sneasler struggled to break through the opponent's dual screens setup and defensive positioning, allowing Serperior and Klefki to clean up the endgame.
reflections.adjustment: Bring Whimsicott to set Tailwind for speed control and use Taunt or Encore to disrupt Klefki's screens and utility moves early.
reflections.notebook: Opponent uses Mega Gengar, Gyarados with Life Orb, Serperior with Expert Belt and Contrary Leaf Storm, and Klefki with Prankster dual screens, Thunder Wave, and Foul Play.
